title: The Base and the Arm as One: A Jacobian With Eight Columns, a Weight on Moving the Base, and a Line Drawn Farther Than the Arm Alone Can Reach

questions.question: Why does the whole body have eight columns and not nine?
options: A differential drive base cannot slide sideways, so it has two rates
The arm has only five joints that move the hand
Two of the nine columns are always equal
The base's height is fixed, which removes one
questions.explanation: Six columns are the arm's joints. The base adds driving along its heading and turning about its centre, and nothing sideways.

questions.question: The arm alone ended how far short of a line of 1.5 m?
options: 0.000 m: it reached the end
questions.explanation: The arm stretched to its full length and stopped there, 1.18 m from the end of the line, with its manipulability at zero.

questions.question: Arm and base together:
options: Reached it, but with the arm at full stretch
Fell 0.07 m short
Reached it only with the base made cheap
Reached it to 0.000 m
questions.explanation: The base drove 1.43 m and the arm's manipulability never fell below 0.0316. The base covered the distance and the arm stayed in the middle of its range.

questions.question: What does a dearer base do?
options: Moves more, to get it over with
Moves the same, and the arm slows down
Moves less, and the arm more
Stops, and leaves the arm to finish
questions.explanation: The weights are prices in a least squares problem. Raise the price of the base's rates and the answer uses more arm: 1.20 m of driving against 1.50 m.

questions.question: Why did the price on the base change the travel so little?
options: The base has to cover the distance the arm cannot, whatever the price
The weights were too close to each other to matter
The damping swamps the weights
The arm is always preferred, whatever the price
questions.explanation: The line was 1.5 m and the arm reaches a fraction of that. Whatever the weights, the base had to drive most of it.

questions.question: What is not in this model?
options: The two rates of the base
The weights on the base and the arm
The base's acceleration and slip, the joint speed limits and obstacles
The arm's manipulability along the line
questions.explanation: The rates come out of a formula with no limits in it. A real base has its own acceleration and slip, and real joints have speed limits.
